questions.q: An integer is chosen at random from the integers $1, 2, 3, . . . . . , 50$. The probability that the chosen integer is a multiple of atleast one of $4, 6$ and $7$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let $A = \left\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, . . . . . . . . . , 50\right\}$

Now, the probability of choosing a number which is a multiple of $4$ will be $P\left(4\right) = \dfrac{12}{50}$

Similarly, the probability of choosing a number which is a multiple of $6$ will be $P\left(6\right) = \dfrac{8}{50}$

And the probability of choosing a number which is a multiple of $7$ will be $P\left(7\right) = \dfrac{7}{50}$

Also, the probability of choosing a number which is a multiple of $4 & 6$ will be $P\left(4 ∩ 6\right) = \dfrac{4}{50}$

And the probability of choosing a number which is a multiple of $6 & 7$ will be $P\left(6 ∩ 7\right) = \dfrac{1}{50}$

And the probability of choosing a number which is a multiple of $4 & 7$ will be $P\left(4 ∩ 7\right) = \dfrac{1}{50}$

And finally, the probability of choosing a number which is a multiple of $4, 6 & 7$ will be $P\left(4 ∩ 6 ∩ 7\right) = 0$

Hence, $P\left(4 ∪ 6 ∪ 7\right) = \dfrac{12}{50} + \dfrac{8}{50} + \dfrac{7}{50} - \dfrac{4}{50} - \dfrac{1}{50} - \dfrac{1}{50} + 0$

$⇒ P\left(4 ∪ 6 ∪ 7\right) = \dfrac{21}{50}$

questions.q: A die is thrown two times and the sum of the scores appearing on the die is observed to be a multiple of $4$. Then the conditional probability that the score $4$ has appeared at least once is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
A die is thrown two times.

Total number of possible outcomes$= 36$.

Let~$E$~is the event that sum of the score appearing on the die is multiple of~$4$.

Possible outcomes in favor of~$E = \left\{\left(1, 3\right), \left(3, 1\right), \left(2, 2\right), \left(2, 6\right), \left(6, 2\right), \left(3, 5\right), \left(5, 3\right), \left(4, 4\right), \left(6, 6\right)\right\}$.

Number of favorable outcomes$= 9$.

$P\left(E\right) = \dfrac{1}{4}$.

Let~$F$~is the event that at least one~$4$~appear.

Possible outcomes in favor of~$F = \left\{\left(1, 4\right), \left(4, 1\right), \left(2, 4\right), \left(4, 2\right), \left(3, 4\right), \left(4, 3\right), \left(4, 4\right), \left(4, 5\right), \left(5, 4\right), \left(4, 6\right), \left(6, 4\right)\right\}$

$E ∩ F = \left\{\left(4, 4\right)\right\}$

$⇒ P\left(E ∩ F\right) = \dfrac{1}{36}$.

We have to find conditional probability of occurrence of at least one~$4$~given that sum of scores is multiple of~$4$.

$P\left(F / E\right) = \dfrac{P\left(E ∩ F\right)}{P\left(E\right)} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{36}}{\dfrac{1}{4}} = \dfrac{1}{9}$.

questions.q: If the probability that the random variable $X$ takes values $x$ is given by $P ( X = x ) = k ( x + 1 ) {3}^{- x}$, $x = 0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots \ldots$, where $k$ is a constant, then $P ( X \ge 2 )$ is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$

Given,

The probability that the random variable $X$ takes values $x$ is given by $P ( X = x ) = k ( x + 1 ) {3}^{- x}$, $x = 0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots \ldots$, where $k$ is a constant,

~Now we know that,

$P ( X = 0 ) + P ( x = 1 ) + P ( x = 2 ) + \ldots \ldots \ldots = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{k}{30} + \dfrac{2k}{31} + \dfrac{3k}{32} + \ldots . . = 1$

$⇒ k\left(1 + \dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{3}{32} + \ldots .\right) = 1$

Now finding,

$S = 1 + \dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{3}{32} + \dfrac{4}{33} + \ldots . . . . \left(1\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{S}{3} = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{2}{32} + \dfrac{3}{32} + \ldots \ldots . . . . . \left(2\right)$

Now on subtracting above two equation we get,

$⇒ $\dfrac{2S}{3} =$1 + $\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{32} + \ldots \ldots

$⇒ S = $\dfrac{9}{4}

Hence,~$k\left(1 + $\dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{3}{32} + \ldots .\right) =$1$

$⇒ k = $\dfrac{4}{9}

Now finding,

~$P ( X \ge 2 ) = P ( 2 ) + P ( 3 ) + \ldots \ldots$

$⇒ P ( X \ge 2 ) = 1 - P ( 0 ) - P ( 1 )$

$⇒ P ( X \ge 2 ) = 1 - \$left(\dfrac{k}{1} + \dfrac{2k}{3}\right) =$1 - $\dfrac{20}{27} = \dfrac{7}{27}

questions.q: Let $A, B$ and $C$ be three events such that the probability that exactly one of $A$ and $B$ occurs is $( 1 - k ) ,$~the probability that exactly one of $B$ and $C$ occurs is $( 1 - 2k ) ,$~the probability that exactly one of $C$ and $A$ occurs is $( 1 - k )$ and the probability of all $A, B$ and $C$ occur simultaneously is $k^{2},$~where $0 < k < 1 .$ Then the probability that at least one of $A, B$ and $C$ occur is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given:

$P ( \overset{¯}{A} ∩ B ) + P ( A ∩ \overset{¯}{B} ) = 1 - k$

$P ( \overset{¯}{A} ∩ C ) + P ( A ∩ \overset{¯}{C} ) = 1 - k$

$P ( \overset{¯}{B} ∩ C ) + P ( B ∩ \overset{¯}{C} ) = 1 - 2k$

$P ( A ∩ B ∩ C ) = k^{2}$

Now,

$P ( A ) + P ( B ) - 2P ( A ∩ B ) = 1 - k \ldots \left(i\right)$

$P ( B ) + P ( C ) - 2P ( B ∩ C ) = 1 - 2k \ldots \left(ii\right)$

$P ( C ) + P ( A ) - 2P ( A ∩ C ) = 1 - k \ldots \left(iii\right)$

Adding~ \left($i\right), \left(ii\right) \text{ and } \left($iii\right)$, we get

P\left($A\right) + $P\left($B\right) + $P\left($C\right) - $P\left($A ∩ B\right) - $P\left($B ∩ C\right) - $P\left($C ∩ A\right) = \dfrac{- 4k + 3}{2}$

Now,

P\left($A ∪ B ∪ C\right) = $P\left($A\right) + $P\left($B\right) + P \left(C\right) - P \left($A ∩ B\right) - P \left(B ∩ C\right) - P\left(C ∩ A\right) + P\left(A ∩ B ∩ C\right)$

$⇒ P\left(A ∪ B ∪ C\right) = \dfrac{- 4k + 3}{2} +k^{2}$

$⇒ P\left(A ∪ B ∪ C\right) = \dfrac{2k^{2} - 4k + 3}{2}$

$⇒ P\left(A ∪ B ∪ C\right) = \dfrac{2 ( k - 1{)}^{2} + 1}{2}$

$⇒ P\left(A ∪ B ∪ C\right) = \left(k - 1\right)2 + \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ P ( A ∪ B ∪ C ) > \dfrac{1}{2}

$

questions.q: Let a computer program generate only the digits $0$ and $1$ to form a string of binary numbers with probability of occurrence of~$0$ at even places be $\dfrac{1}{2}$ and probability of occurrence of $0$ at the odd place be $\dfrac{1}{3} .$ Then the probability that $10$ is followed by $01$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given the probability that the digit& $0$~appear at the even place is~$\dfrac{1}{2},$~hence~the~probability that the digit~$1$~appear at the even place is~$1 - \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} .$

And~the probability that the digit~$0$~appear at the odd~place is~$\dfrac{1}{3},$ hence~the probability that the digit~$1$~appear at the odd~place is~$1 - \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{2}{3} .$

For the digits~$' 10 '$~and~$' 01 '$~we have the following possibilities~

$\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ oddplace & evenplace & oddplace & evenplace\end{cases}$

Or

$\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ evenplace & oddplace & evenplace & oddplace\end{cases}$

Thus, the required probability is~\left(\dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{3} \cdot \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{2}{3}\right) + \left(\dfrac{2}{3} \cdot \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{3} \cdot \dfrac{1}{2}\right)

$= \dfrac{1}{18} + \dfrac{1}{18} = \dfrac{1}{9} .$

Total number of balls in the bag $= 6 + 9 = 15$.

Four balls are drawn at random at a time.

The probability that first draw give four white balls

$\dfrac{C4 6}{C4 15} = \dfrac{1}{91}$

The probability that the first draw give four white balls and second draw give four black balls

$= \dfrac{1}{91} \times \dfrac{21}{55} = \dfrac{3}{715}$

Hence, the required probability is $\dfrac{3}{715}$.

questions.q: $25 %$ of the population are smokers. A smoker has $27$ times more chances to develop lung cancer then a non-smoker. A person is diagnosed with lung cancer and the probability that this person is a smoker is $\dfrac{k}{10}$.Then the value of $k$ is _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

In a city,& $25 %$~of the population is smoker

So,~$P\left(\text{smoker}\right) = 0 . 25$

$P\left(\text{non-smoking}\right) = 0 . 75$

And smoker has~$27$~times more chance of being diagnosed with lung cancer,

So, if~$P\left(\dfrac{Lung cancer}{non-smoker}\right) = p$~then~$P\left(\dfrac{Lung cancer}{smoker}\right) = 27p$,

Now,~ a~person is selected at random and found to be diagnosed with~lung cancer,

So, total~probability of having~a lung cancer will be~

$P\left(\text{Lung cancer}\right) = 0 . 25 \times 27p + 0 . 75 \times p$

So the probability of him being smoker (using bayes' theorem) will be~$P\left(\dfrac{smoker}{Lung cancer}\right) = \dfrac{0 . 25 \times 27p}{0 . 25 \times 27p + 0 . 75 \times p} = \dfrac{27}{30} = \dfrac{9}{10}$

Now comparing with~$\dfrac{k}{10} = \dfrac{9}{10}$,

Then the value of~$k$~will be~$9$.&
